summary: The note surveys how financial markets worldwide approach Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) after a string of breaches in late 2023. It compares regulation (EU, US), vendor assessment methods (Asia, BIS), alliances, AI automation, and staff training. It concludes that regulation, technology, collaboration and human capital will shape financial cybersecurity.
one_line: Overview of how global financial markets handle third-party cyber risk through regulation, vendor assessment, alliances, AI automation and staff training after late-2023 breaches.
key_facts: A breach on October 20, 2023 affected a prominent New York-based bank, causing losses in capital and customer trust.
Jasper Ruiz, cybersecurity consultant and former NSA analyst, said every third-party provider is 'both a necessity and a risk' and a potential backdoor for cybercriminals.
The EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) was updated on September 14, 2023, imposing stringent compliance and incident reporting requirements on data handlers and their vendors.
The United States uses a segmented framework, combining federal directives like FedRAMP with state rules like the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).
Singapore and Hong Kong use robust risk scoring models with continuous monitoring of vendor security practices, per a November 2023 Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) report.
The Bank for International Standards released a memo on December 1, 2023 urging a qualitative approach that engages vendors about their security cultures beyond checklists.
After the September 2023 cyber-attacks, Australia's Big Four banks announced a shared platform for third-party risk assessment to standardize vendor evaluation.
Enrique Morales, a London-based Fintech security expert, highlighted that lack of standardized TPRM practices across borders complicates risk assessment for global firms.
IOSCO works to create a united front addressing international discrepancies in TPRM practices.
US fintech startup Securalyze offers automated vendor assessments using artificial intelligence.
After the system outage of September 15, 2023, the European Banking Authority (EBA) issued guidelines stressing human oversight of AI in decision-making.
The Financial Stability Board and the Association of Banks in Singapore (after its October 2023 symposium) emphasize sustained vendor engagement and continuous monitoring.
Elisabeth O'Connor, a Frankfurt-based cybersecurity trainer, calls employee awareness the first line of defense.
